ICF International (2015). Economic Analysis of Methane Emission Reduction Opportunities in the Canadian Oil and Natural Gas Industries. Report prepared for Environmental Defense Fund, New York, NY (partner: Pembina Institute), September/October 2015. Fairfax, VA: ICF International. 117 pp.

Page numbers are the printed report pages (section-page, e.g. 3-26), not PDF pages. Loaded: every mitigation measure in Table 3-8 (capital, operating cost, percent reduction, cost per Mcf with and without credit for recovered gas), the Table 3-6 VRU size classes, the per-facility LDAR costs and methane reductions of Table 3-4, and the per-unit methane reductions printed in the text (rod packing 438 Mcf/yr, chemical injection pump 180, VRU 9,232 weighted, Kimray pump 5,000). Table 4-1 national totals and study assumptions are in other-values. All costs are Canadian dollars; no price year is printed, so 2015 (publication year) is used; they include a 20% escalation over US Gulf Coast costs, regional adjustments only in the national model. Mcf = thousand cubic feet of methane; the report prints cost per t CO2e only as aggregates, so the coordinator converts per-Mcf values to t CH4. Source inconsistencies kept as printed with both values: Table 3-8 versus text for high-bleed replacement (4,500 vs 4,464), stranded gas flare (94,050 vs 93,750 and 3.17 vs 2.78 per Mcf), pump-down (591,468 vs 590,226), wet seal cost per Mcf (0.48/-7.13 vs 0.4/-5.94), and LDAR cost per Mcf in Table 3-4 versus Table 3-8; Table 3-4 prints 7 Mcf for LDC reduction, 68.4 derived. Gas credits are valued on whole gas. LDAR in Table 3-8 repeats the single-inspector programme capital and labour cost for every segment: recorded once. Not extracted: baseline inventory (appendices A-D), emission projections, regional multipliers, co-benefits.
